drafts.headline: D11 depreciation forecasts run about 2.5 times too low for SWDY.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.931 log (about 2.5 times too low), average miss 0.931, wrong in the same direction in 100% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=30).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.proposed_reason: A PP&E roll-forward that models additions and not the translation of a foreign asset base must under-forecast depreciation on a currency that moves, and the error is arithmetic rather than evidence. Note 17 adds EGP 9,941,876,468 to machinery cost in FY2024 as an exchange movement alone, against additions of EGP 2,061,542,102 — four and a half times the real spend. This is a METHOD defect: every PP&E roll-forward in this book omits the translation term, so it binds on every study with a foreign asset base rather than on this one. It is the reason the correction was refused despite the largest clause-1 improvement any candidate offered.

drafts.headline: D15 finance costs forecasts run about 2.4 times too low for SWDY.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias -0.880 log (about 2.4 times too low), average miss 0.919, wrong in the same direction in 91% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=45).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run of the same name where the sign no longer holds across bootstrap blocks.
drafts.proposed_reason: A finance-cost driver that holds the CHARGE flat is holding the DEBT BOOK flat, and on an issuer whose interest-bearing borrowings went from EGP 6.6bn to EGP 62.5bn — nine and a half times — the 88 log points of 'bias' are the growth of the book. This is [L-002] arriving in a new costume and it is worth registering separately, because [L-002] is about the DENOMINATOR of the rate and this is about the QUANTITY the rate is applied to. The house builds finance cost as rate x interest-bearing borrowings everywhere; a level-persistence rule is inconsistent with that, and the correction it invites would have hidden the inconsistency.

drafts.headline: D1 cable volume t forecasts run about 28% too high for SWDY.
drafts.plain: The method misses this driver in the same direction almost every time, not at random. That is a fixable defect rather than noise — find what is wired wrong before adding any correction factor.
drafts.evidence: Bias +0.250 log (about 28% too high), average miss 0.256, wrong in the same direction in 95% of cases, and the sign holds across every bootstrap block tested (n=20).
drafts.why_scope: A robust bias in one driver may be this company's disclosure, its whole class's economics, or our method. Decide which before filing.

drafts.proposed_reason: Cable tonnage over-forecasts by 28% in nineteen cells of twenty, the ONLY driver in the table that runs the other way, and it LOSES to freeze by 38%. Real GDP is the wrong exogenous anchor for a metal-goods volume: tonnage is rationed by the copper price and by which projects are being wired, not by activity in aggregate. Scoped to the class rather than to ALL because the finding is about a PHYSICAL volume anchored on activity, which is how this book builds a manufacturer and not how it builds a bank or a developer. Filed at the narrower scope on three expanding-window origins — widen it when a second manufacturer shows the same thing.

drafts.headline: The D11 depreciation forecast loses to assuming no change.
drafts.plain: At 5 of 5 horizons, simply carrying last year's number forward beat the model. A method that cannot beat 'no change' has not earned the precision it displays, and should be published as a range or not at all.
drafts.evidence: Negative skill against the freeze benchmark at horizons 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, worst -0.889.
drafts.why_scope: Losing to a naive benchmark usually points at the method, which would make it ALL — but confirm it is not this company's series being unusually persistent.
drafts.overturned_by: A later run where the model beats the freeze benchmark at a majority of horizons.
drafts.proposed_reason: Depreciation losing to freeze is the consequence of the specification defect DRAFT-01 names, not an independent finding about naive benchmarks. Registering it separately would let a reader take it as evidence that the method is weak where it is in fact evidence that one driver is wired wrong.
drafts.declined: Depreciation losing to freeze is the consequence of the specification defect DRAFT-01 names, not an independent finding about naive benchmarks. drafts.headline: The A gross profit error is the company, not the currency.
drafts.plain: Re-running every forecast with perfect foresight of inflation barely improves it. So devaluation is not the explanation, and looking for a macro fix would waste the effort.
drafts.evidence: Average miss 0.563 as known, 0.563 with perfect foresight of inflation — the macro share is only -61.7%.
drafts.why_scope: Almost always ALL — 'check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does' is a method rule — but the specific finding may be about this market.
drafts.overturned_by: A market or period where the same decomposition puts most of the error on the macro path.
drafts.proposed_reason: Perfect foresight of inflation and the currency removes AT MOST 28% of the error on a company whose currency lost eighty-five per cent of its value inside the window. That is the strongest form this negative result has been measured in: if devaluation does not explain the misses HERE, an assumption that it explains them elsewhere needs measuring rather than asserting. The general rule — check whether the macro explains it before assuming it does — is a method rule and binds on every study. This one draft carries the finding; DRAFT-12 through DRAFT-17 are the same measurement on individual drivers.

drafts.headline: The A cost of revenue bias changes direction between regimes.
drafts.plain: It runs one way in one period and the other way in the next. Averaging them produces a correction that is wrong in both. Record it, do not correct for it.
drafts.evidence: By era: pre-float +0.026; first float -0.024; second float -0.460.
drafts.why_scope: A sign that flips with the regime is usually about the market or the period, not the company — but say which.
drafts.overturned_by: A longer record in which one sign dominates across all regimes.
drafts.proposed_reason: The cost-of-revenue bias runs +0.021 before the 2016 float, −0.161 through the first float and −0.538 through the second. A bias that changes direction between regimes is not a bias, and the average of three regimes was true in none of them. Registering ONE instability lesson from this run rather than eight: what generalises is that this book's single largest sample produced five sign-flipping drivers out of nineteen, and that the cut-invariant test [R-FCAL-01 AMENDED 07-09-2026] — not the market's own currency boundary — is what separated them. DRAFT-19 through DRAFT-25 are the same phenomenon on other lines.
